scope: Firestore rules and callable ownership boundaries for AI Adaptive Scheduling
controls: All adaptive paths are nested below users/{uid} and reads enforce request.auth.uid equality.
Behavior events, patterns, suggestions, history, insights, preferences, and push tokens are writable only through trusted Admin SDK functions.
Raw device push tokens cannot be read through the Firestore client.
Activity create and update validate a strict field allowlist, types, sizes, ownership, timestamps, flexibility invariants, and server-calculated fields.
Callable handlers ignore frontend user IDs and derive ownership from verified Firebase Authentication.
Schedule acceptance uses optimistic version/time checks and a Firestore transaction before any state change.
App Check is enforced on all adaptive callable functions.
Rules end with a recursive default deny.
devilsAdvocateTests: Unauthenticated read of another user's suggestion
Direct pattern, behavior, suggestion, history, insight, settings, and push-token writes
Stale suggestion accepted after another-device edit
Conflicting suggestion causing a partial transaction
Adaptive movement of a Google Calendar event

findings.title: Owners can manually edit or delete their own activity records
findings.reason: This is required product behavior. AI-calculated fields remain protected and manual changes invalidate stale suggestions through time/version checks.

findings.title: Admin custom claims can read owner data
findings.reason: This matches the existing support/admin access model; clients cannot grant themselves the signed custom claim.
